entrypoints.summary: The pre-fix website manifest declares ApkUpdatePackageInstallerReceiver with android:exported="true" and no receiver permission.
The receiver accepts broadcast extras for installation status, user-initiated state, and a parcelable nested Intent.

affected_components.role: Pre-fix website-flavor component exposure and fixed exposure state.
Matching attachment URI handling and attachment-stream reads.

negative_controls: The fixed manifest makes the receiver non-exported, but no supplied artifact records a post-fix attempted broadcast or outcome.
observability.positive_marker: The disclosure reports that opening a granted attachment URI returns decrypted attachment bytes.

preconditions: Signal Android website-distribution flavor is installed at an affected version.
A separate attacker-controlled app is installed locally; the disclosure states no declared permissions are required.
The disclosure identifies device/runtime conditions affecting background activity launch and the provider's unlocked/key-caching state.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Broadcast extras selecting the pending-user-action path, with EXTRA_USER_INITIATED true and Intent.EXTRA_INTENT containing an attacker-controlled activity intent, ClipData attachment URI, and read-grant flag.
trigger_steps.summary: Send an explicit broadcast to the exported receiver with attacker-controlled status/user-initiated inputs and a nested Intent selected to carry a delegated read URI grant.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Signal PartProvider single-row content URI identifying an attachment.
trigger_steps.summary: Open the attachment URI delivered through the Signal-mediated intent to cause PartProvider to service the read when its lock check allows it.

capabilities.concept: Untrusted app invocation of package-installer callback
Signal-mediated relaunch of an attacker-controlled URI-granting intent

impacts.concept: Unauthorized read of decrypted Signal attachments

relation_candidates.dst: Untrusted app invocation of package-installer callback
relation_candidates.rationale: The pre-fix website manifest marks the receiver exported, and the disclosure describes it as reachable by another installed application without permissions.

relation_candidates.dst: Signal-mediated relaunch of an attacker-controlled URI-granting intent
relation_candidates.rationale: The receiver reads attacker-controlled broadcast fields, extracts the nested Intent, adds only activity-launch state, and starts it; the disclosure explains preservation of a read-URI-grant flag.
relation_candidates.src: Untrusted app invocation of package-installer callback

relation_candidates.dst: Unauthorized read of decrypted Signal attachments
relation_candidates.rationale: The disclosure ties Signal's URI-permission delegation to opening PartProvider URIs, while provider code opens a matching attachment row through an attachment stream when unlocked.
relation_candidates.src: Signal-mediated relaunch of an attacker-controlled URI-granting intent

relation_candidates.rationale: The fixed website manifest changes this receiver from exported=true to exported=false, removing the untrusted broadcast entry point.
relation_candidates.src: Untrusted app invocation of package-installer callback

impact.affected_asset: Decrypted attachment contents exposed by Signal's PartProvider.
impact.attacker_capability: A separate installed Android app with no declared permissions can, under the disclosure's stated runtime conditions, obtain delegated read access to attachment URIs and read decrypted photos, videos, documents, or voice notes.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized disclosure of decrypted Signal attachments.

causal_trace.summary: The website-distribution manifest exposes ApkUpdatePackageInstallerReceiver to other installed applications without a declared receiver permission.

A broadcast-controlled status and user-initiated boolean select the pending-user-action path, which obtains the nested Intent from Intent.EXTRA_INTENT without validating its target, ClipData, data, or preexisting flags.

The receiver adds FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK and invokes context.startActivity on the attacker-supplied nested Intent; the disclosure reports that a preexisting read-URI-grant flag is preserved, causing Signal to launch the intent and delegate access under Signal's identity.

The disclosure reports that a recipient app can open delegated PartProvider attachment URIs; PartProvider.openFile accepts a matching single-row URI when its locked-state check permits access and returns an attachment stream/proxy whose reads use getAttachmentStream, yielding decrypted attachment data.

failure.operation: context.startActivity(promptIntent) on an unvalidated nested Intent obtained from the incoming broadcast

primary_invariant.statement: An untrusted installed application must not be able to invoke the package-installer callback receiver and cause Signal to launch an attacker-controlled nested Intent with Signal-owned URI permissions.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The website manifest exported the callback receiver, while the receiver trusted broadcast-controlled branch inputs and relaunched the supplied nested Intent after only adding extras and FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK.

quality.review_notes: The coordinated disclosure, vulnerable source, manifest, provider source, and fixed manifest support the stated chain. The bundle has no regression test or observed post-fix execution result, so the remediation is source-diff supported rather than behaviorally verified. Reachability is conditional on the website flavor and the disclosure's Android/runtime and unlocked/key-caching conditions; it should not be generalized to every device state or to Play/GitHub variants.

remediation.invariant_restored: The website flavor no longer exposes ApkUpdatePackageInstallerReceiver to untrusted installed applications, preventing their broadcasts from reaching the nested-Intent relaunch path.
mitigation_classes: removal of untrusted entry to privileged intent relaunch
